decision: WF-110: decide the ticket lifecycle model, the synchronous action set, and whether to build the optional second workflow.

state.workflow: Escalate a converted conversation into an owned ticket (WF-110).

user_flow: Create a Workflow with the trigger 'A ticket is created'.
In the audience/conditions, narrow to the relevant ticket type (e.g. escalation tickets).
Add actions: notify the responsible team in Slack, change the assigned team, apply an SLA, tag the linked conversation.
Optionally add a second Workflow on 'Teammate changes the state of a ticket' to fire when the ticket is closed.
documented_limits: Only background actions are available under this trigger.
Tag conversation, Apply SLA, and Set CDA actions will only work if the ticket acted upon was converted from a conversation.
While using the workflow trigger 'ticket is created' the workflow will not trigger from tracker ticket creation.
events: ticket.resolved fires when a ticket's state transitions to 'resolved'. This is a state-based event.
ticket.closed fires when a ticket conversation is closed. This is separate from state transitions.
ticket.closed nests the Ticket under a ticket field on data.item.

constraints: The owning team is notified when the ticket is created and when its state changes.
WF-107 conversation_chase owns conversation records and is merged; reuse its vocabulary and statuses.
WF-112 (Slack delivery) and WF-108 (SLA timers) may merge later and must not be depended on.
Records are ordinary JSON in records.data. No migration and no typed column.
Every write goes through AuditedDatabase and its audit row names a route the app serves.
The seed must print at least one state that is not a success: a ticket created but with no owning-team notification.

verdict.instructions: Should this build model two separate ticket triggers (ticket-created and state-changed), keep ticket.resolved and ticket.closed as two separate states with two separate webhook payload shapes, treat the synchronous action set as background-only, and encode the tracker-creation exclusion and the converted-conversation gate? Accept only if the model matches the quoted evidence without merging the two events.

criteria.accept: Two triggers, two states, two webhook payload shapes, background-only synchronous actions, tracker exclusion and converted-conversation gate all encoded.
criteria.reject: Merge resolved and closed, or omit a trigger, the tracker exclusion, or the converted-conversation gate.

second_workflow.instructions: The research calls the 'Teammate changes the state of a ticket' workflow optional. Should this build ship it, given that the workflow summary says the owning team is notified when the ticket is created AND when its state changes?

criteria.ship_it: Ship it as a second trigger so a state change notifies the team, which the workflow summary requires.
criteria.omit_it: Ship only the ticket-created trigger, because the research calls the second workflow optional.

is_confident.instructions: Does the quoted evidence support a decisive answer to both questions?

criteria.true: The evidence names the triggers, the events, the limits and the gate directly.
criteria.false: The evidence is close or under-specified.

decision: Implementation of WF-110 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-110 escalates a converted conversation into an owned ticket. The new backend package backend/dsr/conversation_tickets/ models the ticket lifecycle: two triggers (ticket-created and state-changed), two separate terminal states (ticket.resolved as a state transition and ticket.closed as a conversation close, each with its own webhook payload shape), a background-only synchronous action set, the tracker-creation exclusion, and the converted-conversation gate. The feature module backend/dsr/features/wf110_escalate_a_converted_conversation_into_an_owned_ticket.py exposes a router under the unique prefix /api/wf-110 and writes only through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase, so each mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Record payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The frontend feature frontend/src/features/wf-110-conversation-ticket/ ships a page whose default export is discovered by the glob and imports with @/, styled with semantic tokens only.
